messages:
Alex Chen: hey, running into a 403 on prod CI when the pipeline hits the inference endpoint. error from our side: "insufficient_scope: missing permission inference.generate". happened after a key rotation last week. any quick checks?

Maya - Support: ugh. can you paste the curl you used (with obfuscated key) and the full error payload + request_id if you have it? also: is that key created via SSO provisioning or the tokens API?

Alex Chen: here's a scrubbed curl and response: 
```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_API_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  https://api.redwood.com/v1/inference/generate \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hello"}'
```
response: 
```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient_scope",
    "message": "missing permission inference.generate",
    "request_id": "req_8a7f2d"
  }
}
```
Key was generated by a CI job that calls our SSO->token exchange. we rotated some service creds last week in that flow.

Priya Patel: thanks. two quick things: 1) confirm the token scopes via the tokens introspection endpoint or Console UI, 2) if the token is from SSO automated provisioning, check the attribute mapping for scopes. most likely the exchange omitted `inference` scope and only gave `embeddings`/`metrics` etc.

Ivan Ops: +1. you can introspect with the admin API: 
```bash
# admin-only debug, replace TOKENID
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" \n  "https://console.redwood.com/v1/admin/tokens/inspect?token=REDACTED"
```
Look for a `scopes` array in the response. If `inference` is missing, calls to /v1/inference/* will 403.

Maya - Support: also grabbing the audit log for req_8a7f2d. give me a sec.

deploy-bot: Deploy: token-service v1.14.2 -> prod (2026-02-28T18:04:12Z) :rocket:

Maya - Support: audit shows token exchange call from your CI job 2026-03-01T02:11:03Z returned a token with scopes: ["embeddings", "rerank"]. no `inference`. looks like the SSO role mapping changed during the rotation.

Alex Chen: ahhh that explains it. our CI role config in Okta got a new app assignment and the mapping for `inference` was dropped. can you confirm steps to fix without breaking other tokens?

Priya Patel: recommended remediation: 1) update Okta/IdP role->scopes mapping to include `inference` for this service principal, 2) rotate the CI token (re-run your exchange) so new tokens contain the updated scopes, 3) if you need immediate unblock, create a short-lived token manually via Console with scopes `inference,embeddings,rerank` and drop it into CI.

Ivan Ops: CLI snippet to make a manual token (support/ops only): 
```bash
# Create a machine token with the three scopes, 90d expiry
redwood tokens create --name "ci-prod-temp" --scopes inference,embeddings,rerank --expires 90d
# output will be the token value; update your CI secret and redeploy
```

Alex Chen: trying manual token now. will swap in and kick pipeline.

Maya - Support: re: long-term: we should add a warning in the Console and logs when a token is missing a scope that a request attempted to use. filing a feature request. also attaching the audit link: https://console.redwood.com/audit/req_8a7f2d (internal)

Alex Chen: manual token worked, pipeline succeeded and inference calls are green. huge thanks. also leaving a note in our Okta app config to prevent future drops. :thumbsup:

Priya Patel: glad it's fixed. we'll follow up with a short runbook for SSO->token mapping pitfalls and add an internal postmortem for this one.

Ivan Ops: FYI added a short-lived playbook entry to the ops-runbook: "if inference 403 -> inspect scopes -> check IdP mapping -> rotate token".

Maya - Support: closing the support ticket, will attach runbook + audit snapshot. reopen if anything else pops.

Alex Chen: thanks all, appreciate the quick turnaround!
